subject: Heritage Bank implementation questionnaire: appliance swarm integration & rollback protocol
messages:
From: Anita Chowdhury <anita.chowdhury@heritagebank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@heritagebank.com>, procurement@heritagebank.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: RFP: Implementation questions (appliance/hybrid options)

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The RFP committee had a few follow-up questions specifically around your 'appliance swarm' option and how Redwood would handle phased cutovers across 3 data centers. I've attached our implementation questionnaire (sheet 2 contains the timeline we expect). High level asks:

- Deployment model: can you run a private appliance + cloud hybrid where traffic shards route to appliance first?
- Integration contracts: required API endpoints and expected SLAs for retries/backoff.
- Canary and rollback: recommended canary size, telemetry gates, and exact rollback triggers.
- Security/compliance: audit/log retention during switchover and key custody model.

Can you send a short runbook and a proposed 8-week timeline by Dec 6? Procurement will want an entry for the implementation milestones to align payment milestones.

Attachments: HB_RFP_implementation_questions.xlsx (sheet: Implementation)

Best,
-Anita Chowdhury
Sr. Program Manager, Cloud Migration
Heritage Bank

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Anita Chowdhury <anita.chowdhury@heritagebank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-23T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Implementation questions (appliance/hybrid options)

Anita —

Thanks for the clear list. We put together a focused response and an initial runbook that maps to your 8-week window. Core summary below; full runbook attached (redwood-implementation-runbook-v1.pdf) plus a machine-readable API contract (api-contracts-v2.json). Key points: 

1) Deployment model
- Hybrid supported: appliances act as primary route for customer-controlled traffic shards; cloud nodes are configured as warm fallback for overflow.
- Appliances run Redwood Private runtime (signed binaries) behind the customer's network boundary; control-plane connections to Redwood control plane are optional — we support an offline mode with signed manifests for upgrades.

2) Timeline (8-week example)
- Week 0 (prep): procurement intake, network whitelisting, key exchange, provisioning POCs (2 appliances)
- Weeks 1–2 (integration): API contract validation, mutual auth, test harness against sandbox
- Week 3 (canary stage): enable 5% production shards to appliances in DC-1; telemetry baseline collection
- Weeks 4–5 (scale): expand to DC-2 with 20% shards then DC-3 to 50% while monitoring QPS/latency/cost metrics
- Week 6 (verification): run performance regressions and failover drills; security audit snapshot
- Week 7 (cutover): schedule maintenance window, flip traffic to appliances primary for low-risk routes
- Week 8 (wrap): finalize runbook, handoff SOPs to Heritage ops, payment milestone sign-off

3) Canary & rollback policy (recommended)
- Initial canary: 5% of sessions, minimum 50 concurrent sessions or 5k tokens/min, whichever first.
- Gates (fail if any met): 20% sustained latency increase vs baseline >3 minutes, error rate >1.5% over 5 minutes, or model-quality regression flagged by your eval set.
- Automatic rollback: control-plane will drain canary traffic to previous routing in <90s; appliances execute hot rollback with KV-cache flush policy described in runbook.

4) Telemetry & audit
- We ship per-token telemetry to your SIEM via secure syslog or Kafka connector; retention policy during cutover is configurable (default 90d).
- All admin operations on appliances are logged with KMS-wrapped keys; we provide audit export as NDJSON on request.

5) Security/compliance artifacts
- SOC2 Type II summary, penetration-test overview, and KMS integration guide included in the Drive link below.

Next steps I propose: quick alignment call (30m) with your platform team + our delivery DRI (Karthik) and integration lead (Priyom) to lock the weeks and canary thresholds. Are you available Mon/Dec 7 or Tue/Dec 8 (morning PST)?

Attachments: redwood-implementation-runbook-v1.pdf; api-contracts-v2.json

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-24T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Heritage Bank - canary thresholds and ops DRIs

Folks —

Quick notes before the alignment call:
- Canary sizing: suggest lowering the initial session floor to 25 concurrent sessions for low-traffic routes. Anita's plan lists some low-traffic workloads that will never hit 50 concurrent. We'll gate on tokens/min as well.
- Rollback mechanics: appliances will support two rollback modes: immediate drain (fast path, client-side reconnect) and graceful stepdown (drain with KV snapshot). For financial workloads we default to graceful stepdown.
- DRIs: Karthik (deployment orchestration), Priyom (sandbox/integration), Laura (security attestations).

I'll propose these items on the call and ask for explicit acceptance per workload. Also flag: we need to confirm NTP/clock sync requirements (Heritage must allow NTP to our monitored endpoint or provide screenshot of internal NTP sync) — otherwise audit exports will have gaps.

-K

From: Anita Chowdhury <anita.chowdhury@heritagebank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@heritagebank.com>, procurement@heritagebank.com
Date: 2026-11-30T14:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Implementation questions (appliance/hybrid options)

Marissa,

Thanks for the thorough response and the runbook. A few clarifications from the platform team: 

- For low-traffic shards we accept the 25-concurrent-sessions floor. Please include a tokens/miner metric as secondary gate.
- Can you provide an exported sample of the telemetry NDJSON (anonymized) so our observability team can validate schema mapping to Splunk?
- Procurement asked to split the implementation payment into three milestones tied to Week 3 (canary), Week 6 (verification), Week 8 (wrap). Is that acceptable to Redwood?

We can meet on Tue/Dec 8 at 09:00 PST for the alignment call. Please add Karthik and Priyom.

Regards,
Anita

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Anita Chowdhury <anita.chowdhury@heritagebank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, partner@cloudops.io
Date: 2026-12-05T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Implementation questions (appliance/hybrid options)

Anita —

Perfect. Agreed on the 25-session floor + tokens/min secondary gate. Procurement milestone split is acceptable. I'll attach an anonymized telemetry sample in the shared Drive (see link) and include a short CSV checklist for your SRE on the call. For the call agenda I propose:

1) Introductions & roles (5m)
2) Walkthrough: runbook milestones & live demo of sandbox connectivity (10m)
3) Canary policy: thresholds & monitoring dashboards (10m)
4) Ops: rollback modes, KMS exchange steps, NTP requirement (10m)
5) Procurement: payment milestones & acceptance criteria (5m)

Attachments: heritage_canary_checklist.csv (small ops checklist). Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleRunbook

Look forward to Tuesday. Meeting invite sent.

- Marissa
